MAJOR ARCANA

The Magician — Meaning

Major Arcana

  • CategoryMajor Arcana
  • SymbolMercury / Number 1
  • UprightWhat you can do, Resourcefulness, Action
  • ReversedAll talk, Spinning wheels, Underprepared

A card about using the abilities and tools already in your hands.

The Magician stands for "What you can do, Resourcefulness, Action" when upright, and "All talk, Spinning wheels, Underprepared" when reversed. Before gathering new things, look at the knowledge and tools you already have. Combined well, they may be enough to begin.

Reading it in a decision — When starting a side job or new work, read this card as looking for a step you can begin today by combining the skills, tools, and people you already have, before buying what is missing. Reversed, use it to check whether presentation and explanation are running ahead while your hands stay still.

The decision this speaks to: When you're torn about starting a side job

SYMBOLS

The symbols in the picture

On the table lie a wand, a cup, a sword, and a coin. The magician points one hand to the sky and the other to the earth — turning what you are thinking into shape with the tools at hand.

UPRIGHT

Upright meaning

  • What you can do
  • Resourcefulness
  • Action

Before gathering new things, look at the knowledge and tools you already have. Combined well, they may be enough to begin.

Reversed meaning

FOR YOUR DECISION

Hints for your decision

How to read it when you are deciding

The Magician depicts a state where the tools you need are already laid out on the table. When you are torn about a decision, rather than counting what is missing, turn your eyes to how you can combine the skills, connections, and time you already have. The four tools on the table are said to represent will, feeling, thought, and reality. Checking whether you lean too far toward just one of them is also useful. Reversed, it can indicate a plan running ahead in words only, while the hands are not moving.

How to face a familiar worry

This card often appears when you want to start something with your own power — a project, a side job. If you are torn, set a deadline and make a prototype first. Having something you can show others multiplies your material for judging at once. Reversed, rebuild trust by keeping one promise reliably, rather than polishing your explanation.

Questions to ask yourself before you decide

Are the tools to make this choice real already laid out on your table? Is what is missing the materials, or the resolve to start using them? Can you explain the plan in your own words in one minute? Is there even one move you can make today to begin?

"Ease of moving forward" is the strength of the tailwind behind an option if you move on it now — not a judgment of whether things will turn out well or badly.

Now that you have read the meaning, turn to the decision in front of you. Draw a card and lay your two options side by side.
